title: Light frames · Silhouette studies
summary: Lacewing catches a left dash with one back launcher open. The pose studies develop the center mech in the original three-frame lineup below.

items.title: Lacewing · Catching the left dash
items.alt: An olive insect mech catches its weight on three left toes, its other foot tucked. A blue hip jet fades beneath one raised plum launcher shell. A forked projector and a ceramic pulse ram point forward.
items.body:
**Current pose study.** The left foot catches the slide while the right leg stays tucked. The paired recessed rear exhausts sit above the cockpit hatch. A separate jet on the right hip marks the direction of the lateral boost.

One plum case follows the back while the raised case exposes its launch cells. The stowed case houses the proposed beam weapon. The forked arc projector and nested ceramic pulse ram are angled toward the same target. Their silhouettes overlap slightly from this camera position.

Built-in image generation revised the first dash study below. [Open full-resolution PNG](assets/light-frames/lacewing-left-dash-v002.png)
items.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Revise the supplied Lacewing dash painting as the same instant and same exact mech. Make the gameplay chase angle, the shell asymmetry and the aim of the weapons immediately readable. 
(1) Lower and fully furl the SMALLER LEFT BACK COVER (picture left) across the back. Rotate this articulated cover and the inactive beam unit down; stow it FLUSH along the left edge of the olive back, its pointed plum tip extending DOWN toward the left hip. It should read as a narrow smooth overlapping carapace on the back; no second tall spike protruding upward, and the left rear exhaust must stay clear. The large shell on picture RIGHT alone remains lifted, with its bank of launch cells visible below a petrol-violet inner surface. The right launcher and its lid remain prominent. Keep the lean olive thorax and the small paired recessed rear exhausts; the visible right hip nozzle still sends a fading blue jet to picture right. 
(2) Recompose the camera a little further toward the mech’s rear-right flank, giving a rear THREE-QUARTER perspective rather than a flat view. Show the mech ALREADY AIMED onward across the apron, toward a point in the middle distance at the LEFT third of the distant wall. Show a little side profile of the angular insect sensor head looking there. Bend elbows; bring the two oversized weapons forward so they both face into the depth toward this ONE point instead of pointing outward in opposite directions. Keep the long forked arc projector with separated prongs and field rings in the left hand, and the broad nested-ceramic pulse ram braced close to the right forearm to leave the hip jet free. Keep each gun’s recognizable shape and its weight, and retain a trace of both mechanical grippers. Allow foreshortening, no extra arms, weapons or shockwaves.
(3) Preserve the leftward translation and the level torso; flex the planted LEFT knee a little more, foreshortening the leg under load. Left foot retains contact with the dusty concrete while the right leg floats, tightly folded, clearly off the ground. Preserve the original tapering long insect legs, worn olive skin and dark wrinkled knee sleeves. 
Both the open case and the loaded leg should be readable at first glance. Single full-body wide landscape keyframe, complete shell tips, all feet and both weapons inside frame. Keep the dull concrete yard, scale cues, industrial patina, diffuse sky light, faded olive, brass and plum, and the first painting's detailed restrained brushwork. No text or HUD.

items.body:

items.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve game concept painting, pose and equipment development. The attached reference contains THREE designs. Use ONLY the olive-and-plum INSECT BIPED IN THE CENTER, Lacewing, as the identity reference. Produce one new landscape painting of this single pilotable mech from a rear three-quarter gameplay camera right after a hard LEFT lateral boost. This is a faithful new view and upgraded loadout of the center character: smooth tapered olive thorax with small bolted cockpit hatch, segmented narrow waist, small angular insectoid sensor head, elegant long digitigrade legs with brass joint cups and narrow forked feet, two independently hinged pointed elytra over the upper back. Keep that distinct insect silhouette, folded S-shaped legs, quiet curved armor plates, patina and slim proportions. One mech only. 
Design one immediately readable held instant: the camera is behind, just a little to the mech's right, so machine left is screen left. The mech still faces away, toward the far end of a weathered concrete apron, with the olive cockpit and shoulder axis LEVEL and the weapon arms steady. Its left leg extends sideways and downward to catch its drifting weight on three spread metal toes anchored into the ground, matte black flexible skin creasing behind that loaded knee. The opposite right knee tucks up and in, foot visibly clear of the ground by at least a shin length, leaving daylight beneath it. A thin sideways scrape of pale grit behind the planted foot and the fading flame shooting horizontally OUT to the right from the right hip explain the LEFT strafe. No sprinting stride. The legs are fine-limbed but robust at the hocks, obviously capable of walking and carrying the loaded cockpit. The biological hint lives in the spring of the articulated limbs and dark elastic joint sleeves. Never bare flesh, feminine anatomy or a human face.
The two separated back weapons are integral to the split shell silhouette: the LEFT slim pointed shell stays folded tight along the back over its beam weapon, a glimpse of that weapon's distinct cased tip remains visible. The RIGHT lid lifts high to reveal its rich petrol-violet inner surface and its own compact fan of dark launch cells. Faded olive-green outer carapace, flashes of worn iridescent plum on sheltered edges. Open and closed look very different in silhouette; exactly two shell covers in total. Beneath their hinges, two slim, separate rear-facing recessed exhaust slots stay visible, clear of the upper weapons. The small outward-facing right hip thruster is physically distinct from these rear slots. Its short pale-blue jet is dissipating. No rocket backpack or long fire trails.
One genuinely mech-sized abstract weapon visibly gripped in EACH of two articulated hands on broad wrist cuffs. On frame LEFT, a substantial long FORKED ARC PROJECTOR nearly the length of the whole arm, long parallel insulated tines around an empty gap, suspended field rings and a heavy breech. On frame RIGHT, a broad blunt PULSE RAM with a conspicuous cockpit-hatch-sized striking face of THREE nested off-white ceramic blocks on a stout dark body. Brace both imposing weapons close to the forearms, hold them away from the hips, angle them enough to keep their shapes separately readable. The hands are small relative to these powerful tools. Exactly four weapons counting the two back mounts. No knife, conventional pistol or tiny sidearm.
Grounded grimdark industrial art direction. Cropped-off distant low retaining walls, a human-sized maintenance door, flush drains and expansion joints on an empty apron quietly establish scale. Overcast raking light, bone-gray concrete, warm olive and oxidized brass, charcoal folds and restrained glancing violet. A premium painterly mechanical design keyframe with ink-and-gouache precision, materially convincing and restrained texture. Single wide landscape composition, entire mech AND equipment fit with comfortable margin at every edge, articulated load-bearing silhouette clear at thumbnail size, high contrast against a pale background. No labels, letters, borders, captions, HUD, pilots outside or secondary figures.

items.title: Effigy, Lacewing and Lurcher
items.alt: Three light combat frames in the same scale, from left to right: an upright pale-faced figure, a green insect-like biped with plum wing cases, and a crouching red-gray hound-shaped biped.
items.body:
**Effigy · left.** Charcoal sleeves follow the thighs into exposed knee bearings. Oxidized collar plates frame a pale, nearly human mask. The small face and narrow parallel back mounts preserve a tall silhouette. The face reads quite literally in this painting. A shallower brow and a service slit in place of the mouth would make the expression harder to place.

**Lacewing · center.** Two plum-colored shell covers make a fork above the green cockpit. Each cover opens independently over a back weapon. Both hands remain free to carry a loadout. In motion, the leading knee could straighten smoothly while the thin heel stays planted a beat longer than expected. Try a dark flexible sleeve across that knee to bring the limb references into the design. This is the recommended frame for a second drawing from the chase camera.

**Lurcher · right.** A long muzzle, arched cockpit cage and dropped wrists carry the eye forward over two bent legs. The low back mounts follow the spine. A boost could pitch the entire body forward while the hands skim the ground. The barrels shown here point aft in their stowed position. Their deployed silhouette still needs a rear-view study.

The worn metal, faded markings and recessed fittings take cues from the heavier grimdark models. For a clearer sense of vehicle scale, try a pilot-sized access step beside the cockpit in the next drawing.

[Open full-resolution PNG](assets/light-frames/lineup-v001.png)
items.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Deliver a single landscape concept designer's comparison plate of THREE DISTINCT ORIGINAL, PILOTABLE LIGHT MECHS for a fast grimdark action game. It should look like a published industrial design exploration sheet: match the painting finish, scale, neutral lighting and camera, give each frame a different, instantly memorable black silhouette. Three full-body front three-quarter views side by side, left to right as specified, on warm pale gray paper with only contact shadows, generous breathing room around silhouettes, no overlap, no cropping. Very wide landscape composition. Sharp, controlled gouache and graphite rendering, restrained realistic reflections, deep but readable shadows. Unlabelled artwork. Machine details intentionally selective: bold large forms, skin-like folds at load-bearing joints, metal seams ending at moving parts. A human-scale bolted access hatch on each enclosed torso supplies scale. Each is several metres tall, with two articulated gripper hands, two arms and two main legs and a narrow clear waist. No bulky rectangular torsos, huge pauldrons, bare flesh, human skulls, muscles glued onto armor, tentacle tangles, spikes everywhere, giant backpacks, grim scenery, logos, text, titles, letters, or HUD. The uncanny effect is carried by silhouette, posture and proportions. All retain the ability to equip one weapon per hand and two compact independent back weapons. Keep the four mounts integrated into the silhouette. The PRIMARY subject is the frame design and subtle biomechanical anatomy.
LEFT, EFFIGY: The most striking portrait. Eerily upright tall frame with level, narrow shoulders and a long uninterrupted drop to the feet. Long near-human thighs and calves wrapped in smooth charcoal graphite-colored flexible material that meets exposed round mechanical knee bearings and steel heel pieces, ankle buckling into a tiny convincing compressed fold. Small matte warm-chalk ceramic mask in a dark petrol collar, with two shallow brow shadows, one offset optic and a small horizontal breather low on the face, so it has a restrained ambiguous human expression. Thin backward-fanning crescent of THREE small stacked oxidized bronze neck plates on each side frame the face like folded gills. Compact vertical wedge-shaped sealed torso; narrow, visibly mechanical waist. Upper back carries two slim DIFFERENT weapon spines on close parallel independent rails rising just past the shoulders, head easily visible in between. Right hand holds a short dark sidearm, left a slim straight single-edged dueling blade held low. Both weapons spaced away from the calves. Achieve unnerving stillness by turning the head ten degrees while the pelvis and planted feet face forward; one heel just peeling up. Predominantly soot, aged teal and a small startling pale face. Never an android woman or bodysuit.
CENTER, LACEWING: very different anatomy, deep S-curve and compact diving posture. Articulated wasp-like three-dimensional kiln-green pilot thorax; segmented thin waist supporting a short sealed abdomen; two long folded digitigrade legs in tarnished brass hinge cups, narrow forked mechanical contact feet. Two hard iridescent dark plum elytra partly raised and swept BEHIND the body like a narrow swallowtail V, visible blade-thin edges and hinge roots. Each cover shelters one distinct compact back weapon, a slim gun tube visible under one opened cover and a small launch cassette visible under the other. No flight wings spanning the page. Angular small insect sensor head, no human mask here. Two conventional hand assemblies are posed outboard of the thorax: a short foil-shaped weapon in one and a compact pistol-shaped weapon in the other. Asymmetric stance with one heel raised. Insect shell sheen in controlled patches, dry black armature. No huge beetle shoulders, extra legs or antenna clutter.
RIGHT, LURCHER: a long, low, very lean coursing-hound silhouette in a biped's ready stance, spine cantilevered forward almost horizontally above folded powerful hind legs. Smooth long dog-hock arcs in matte smoke-black skin around mechanical joints, cupped steel toes. Elongated blind wedge-shaped sensor muzzle projects straight ahead from a ribbed, industrial shoulder bridge; recessed lenses at the sides. Four curved metal struts enclose a compact armored pilot pod behind the neck. Skeletal intent with a solid cockpit. Two long, loose forearms hang almost to the knees but BOTH hands and the pair of light handheld weapons (stubby impact pistol and a hooked short blade) are CLEAR of the floor. Two independent slender weapon casings stow low along opposite sides of the upper back like greyhound flanks; one locks up by a few degrees so the separate mount reads. Streaks of worn iron red across warm gray armature, black joints, ears absent. One foot forward, balanced as if it just heard something. Distinguish Lurcher's low horizontal thrust line from the vertical figure on the left and upswept folded-shell geometry at center. No shared generic human chest on all three.
